arxiv-1709-03096.title: Survivable Probability of SDN-enabled Cloud Networking with Random Physical Link Failure
arxiv-1709-03096.creator: Zhili Zhou, Tachun Lin
arxiv-1709-03096.description: Abstract Software-driven cloud networking is a new paradigm in orchestrating physical resources (CPU, network bandwidth, energy, storage) allocated to network functions, services, and applications, which is commonly modeled as a cross-layer network. This model carries a physical network representing the physical infrastructure, a logical network showing demands, and logical-to-physical node/link mappings.

arxiv-2105-13634.title: Saudi Parents’ Privacy Concerns about Their Children’s Smart Device Applications
arxiv-2105-13634.creator: Eman Alashwali, Fatimah Alashwali
arxiv-2105-13634.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate Saudi parents’ privacy concerns regarding their children’s smart device applications (apps). To this end, we conducted a survey and analysed 119 responses. Our results show that Saudi parents expressed a high level of concern regarding their children’s privacy when using smart device apps.

arxiv-2106-01436.title: Black hole induced spins from hyperbolic encounters in dense clusters
arxiv-2106-01436.creator: Santiago Jaraba, Juan García-Bellido
arxiv-2106-01436.description: Abstract The black holes that have been detected via gravitational waves (GW) can have either astrophysical or primordial origin. Some GW events show significant spin for one of the components and have been assumed to be astrophysical, since primordial black holes are generated with very low spins.

arxiv-2107-05419.title: A New Approach for Active Automata Learning Based on Apartness Thanks: Research supported by NWO TOP project 612.001.852 “Grey-box learning of Interfaces for Refactoring Legacy Software (GIRLS)”. Affiliation: Institute for Computing and Information Sciences,
arxiv-2107-05419.creator: Frits Vaandrager ✉ {}^{\text{{\char 12\relax}}}, Bharat Garhewal, Jurriaan Rot, Thorsten Wißmann
arxiv-2107-05419.description: Abstract We present L # L^{\#} , a new and simple approach to active automata learning. Instead of focusing on equivalence of observations, like the L ∗ L^{\ast} algorithm and its descendants, L # L^{\#} takes a different perspective: it tries to establish apartness , a constructive form of inequality.

arxiv-2206-02782.title: Towards Job-Transition-Tag Graph for a Better Job Title Representation Learning
arxiv-2206-02782.creator: Jun Zhu, Céline Hudelot
arxiv-2206-02782.description: Abstract Works on learning job title representation are mainly based on Job-Transition Graph , built from the working history of talents. However, since these records are usually messy, this graph is very sparse, which affects the quality of the learned representation and hinders further analysis.

arxiv-2209-07522.title: Test-Time Training with Masked Autoencoders
arxiv-2209-07522.creator: Yossi GandelsmanUC Berkeley, Yu SunUC BerkeleyXinlei ChenMeta AIAlexei A. EfrosUC Berkeley
arxiv-2209-07522.description: Abstract Test-time training adapts to a new test distribution on the fly by optimizing a model for each test input using self-supervision. In this paper, we use masked autoencoders for this one-sample learning problem. Empirically, our simple method improves generalization on many visual benchmarks for distribution shifts. Theoretically, we characterize this improvement in terms of the bias-variance trade-off.

arxiv-2212-13963.title: First-principles study of spin orbit coupling contribution to anisotropic magnetic interaction
arxiv-2212-13963.creator: Di Wang, Xiangyan Bo, Feng Tang, Xiangang Wan
arxiv-2212-13963.description: Abstract Anisotropic magnetic exchange interactions lead to a surprisingly rich variety of the magnetic properties. Considering the spin orbit coupling (SOC) as perturbation, we extract the general expression of a bilinear spin Hamiltonian, including isotropic exchange interaction, antisymmetric Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction and symmetric Γ \Gamma term.

arxiv-2310-13296.title: Trotterization in Quantum Theory
arxiv-2310-13296.creator: Physics Claire Kluber
arxiv-2310-13296.description: Abstract Abstract Trotterization in quantum mechanics is an important theoretical concept in handling the exponential of noncommutative operators. In this communication, we give a mathematical formulation of the Trotter Product Formula, and apply it to basic examples in which the utility of Trotterization is evident.

arxiv-2312-15748.title: Nondeterministic Infinite Time Turing Machines
arxiv-2312-15748.creator: Erin Carmody
arxiv-2312-15748.description: Abstract . This paper analyzes infinitary nondeterministic computability theory. The main result is D ≠ \neq ND ∩ \cap coND where D is the class of sets decidable by infinite time Turing machines and ND is the class of sets recognizable by a nondeterministic infinite time Turing machine. Nondeterministic infinite time Turing machines are introduced, along with relevant definitions. 1.

arxiv-2402-08485.title: On a Ramanujan-type series associated with the Heegner number 163
arxiv-2402-08485.description: Abstract Using the Wolfram NumberTheory package and the Recognize command, together with numerical estimates involving the elliptic lambda and elliptic alpha functions, Bagis and Glasser, in 2013, introduced a conjectural Ramanujan-type series related to the class number h ⁡ ( − d ) = 1 h(-d)=1 for a quadratic form with discriminant d = 163 d=163 .

arxiv-2403-04109.title: Using Causal Trees to Estimate Personalized Task Difficulty in Post-Stroke Individuals
arxiv-2403-04109.creator: Nathaniel Dennler, Stefanos Nikolaidis, & Maja Matarić
arxiv-2403-04109.description: Abstract Adaptive training programs are crucial for recovery post stroke. However, developing programs that automatically adapt depends on quantifying how difficult a task is for a specific individual at a particular stage of their recovery. In this work, we propose a method that automatically generates regions of different task difficulty levels based on an individual’s performance.

arxiv-2406-04728.title: Monotonic Decompositions of Submodular Set Functions
arxiv-2406-04728.creator: Kristóf Bérczi, Boglárka Gehér, András Imolay, László Lovász, Tamás Schwarcz
arxiv-2406-04728.description: Abstract Submodular set functions are undoubtedly among the most important building blocks of combinatorial optimization. Somewhat surprisingly, continuous counterparts of such functions have also appeared in an analytic line of research where they found applications in the theory of finitely additive measures, nonlinear integrals, and electric capacities.

arxiv-2503-08067.title: Context-aware Biases for Length Extrapolation
arxiv-2503-08067.creator: Ali Veisi, Hamidreza Amirzadeh, Amir Mansourian
arxiv-2503-08067.description: Abstract Transformers often struggle to generalize to longer sequences than those seen during training—a limitation known as length extrapolation. Most existing Relative Positional Encoding (RPE) methods attempt to address this by introducing either fixed linear biases or globally learned biases, which lack the capacity to adapt to different input contexts.

arxiv-2509-07785.title: Algorithmic differentiation for plane-wave DFT: materials design, error control and learning model parameters
arxiv-2509-07785.creator: Niklas Frederik Schmitz, Bruno Ploumhans, Michael F. Herbst
arxiv-2509-07785.description: Abstract We present a differentiation framework for plane-wave density-functional theory (DFT) that combines the strengths of algorithmic differentiation (AD) and density-functional perturbation theory (DFPT). In the resulting AD-DFPT framework derivatives of any DFT output quantity with respect to any input parameter (e.g. geometry, density functional or pseudopotential) can be computed accurately without deriving gradient expressions by hand.

arxiv-2509-17911.title: Chromaticity of stellar activity in radial velocities
arxiv-2509-17911.creator: P. Larue, X. Delfosse, A. Carmona, N. Meunier, É. Artigau, S. Bellotti, P. Charpentier, C. Moutou, J.-F. Donati, I. Boisse, T. Forveille, L. Arnold V. Bourrier, X. arxiv-2509-17911.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by P. Larue, X. Delfosse, A. Carmona, N. Meunier, É. Artigau, S. Bellotti, P. Charpentier, C. Moutou, J.-F. Donati, I. Boisse, T. Forveille, L. Arnold V. Bourrier, X. Bonfils, C. Cadieux, A. Chomez, N. Cook, P. Cortes Zuleta, P. Cristofari, R. Diaz, R. Doyon, S. Grouffal, N. Hara, N. Heidari, G. Hébrar. In the search for exoplanets using radial velocities (RV), stellar activity has become one of the main limiting factors for detectability. Fortunately, activity-induced RV signals are wavelength-dependent or chromatic, unlike planetary signals.

arxiv-2512-01233.description: Abstract . Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions represent a powerful experiential learning approach within cybersecurity education, blending diverse concepts into interactive challenges. However, the short duration (typically 24-48 hours) and ephemeral infrastructure of these events often impede sustained educational benefit.

pmc-10651919.title: Freezing tolerance and tolerance to de-acclimation of European accessions of winter and facultative barley
pmc-10651919.creator: Magdalena Wójcik-Jagła, Marcin Rapacz
pmc-10651919.description: Due to global warming, winter hardiness may seem to become less important for plant survival and yield. However, this is a superficial assumption, as probably only the most important factors locally affecting plant overwintering will change. For example, the frequency, degree, and length of extreme winter warming events may increase, leading to de-acclimation of plants.

pmc-10709557.title: Thermal reaction products and formation pathways of two monoterpenes under in situ thermal desorption conditions that mimic vaping coil temperatures
pmc-10709557.creator: Jianjun Niu, Jiping Zhu
pmc-10709557.description: Vaping has become more popular and different brands and types of vaping devices have rapidly emerged. However, little is known about the potential health risks of human inhalation exposures to the volatile chemicals in the vapour, which includes both directly vaporised components of vaping liquid and their reaction products formed during vaping processes.

pmc-10803671.title: Persian Translation and Determining the Validity of 2020 Standards for Health-Promoting Hospitals and Health Services Affiliated with the World Health Organization

pmc-10803671.description: Background:Since the establishment of the International Health Promotion Hospitals (HPH) in 2006, standards have been designed to evaluate this network. pmc-11688996.title: HEALTH OUTCOMES OF AGING INDIVIDUALS EXPOSED TO HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS IN SOUTH FLORIDA
pmc-11688996.creator: Rebecca Koszalinski, Malcolm McFarland, Michael Parsons, John Reif, Adam Schaefer, Judyta Kociolek
pmc-11688996.description: Environmental changes have profoundly altered the lives of individuals in South Florida. Harmful Algal Blooms (HAB) and associated toxins produced by cyanobacteria and Karenia brevis impact the lives of Floridians, including aging individuals who recreate on the water in their retirement years.

pmc-12511602.title: HSPA4 restrains transferrin in dopaminergic neurons to attenuate ferroptosis in a Parkinson’s disease model
pmc-12511602.creator: Tong Gao, Huanhuan Wei, Qianqian Ju, Yongqi Lin, Xiang Yin, Xiaoyu Liu, Jianhong Shen, Qiuhong Ji, Cheng Sun, Lihua Shen
pmc-12511602.description: Heat shock protein A4 (HSPA4) is a molecular chaperone belonging to the heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) family. This study aims to investigate the antiferroptotic effects of HSPA4 in a Parkinson’s disease (PD) model and explore the underlying mechanisms. Here we show that HSPA4 overexpression reduces ferroptosis in erastin-treated SH-SY5Y cells and primary dopaminergic neurons, while HSPA4 knockdown exacerbates ferroptosis.

pmc-12894255.title: Exploring coronary microvascular dysfunction from functional impairment and structural damage
pmc-12894255.creator: Wei Wen, Yiqing Zhang, Genlin Jia, Yi Chi
pmc-12894255.description: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a syndrome characterized by myocardial ischemia resulting from structural and/or functional impairments of the coronary microvasculature, which includes pre-arterioles, arterioles, and capillaries. It has taken center stage in cardiovascular research due to its established role in triggering heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).

pmc-12929487.title: Tests of large language models' medical competence and application for clinical decision support of musculoskeletal rehabilitation
pmc-12929487.creator: Ruikang Liu, Qiaoling Liu, Qiang Hu, Ruixing Nan, Jian He, Jinru Yang, Jialin Zhang, Guang Yang, Zhaohui Yang, Xiling Xiao, Xiaoxuan Xia, Yongchao Wu
pmc-12929487.description: ObjectiveLarge language models (LLMs) are currently abundant and diverse, yet clinicians lack clarity on top performers, with uncertainty about general LLMs' expertise in musculoskeletal rehabilitation. This study aims to investigate the potential and correctness of LLMs in clinical application, and to evaluate whether LLMs could assist primary rehabilitation therapists to prepare for rehabilitation examination.

pmc-13145602.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A656 ACCEPTABILITY OF DEFERRED CONSENT AMONG PARTICIPANTS AND PROXIES OF AN ACUTE NEUROSURGICAL INTERVENTION TRIAL IN INTRACEREBRAL HAEMORRHAGE; A DUTCH ICH SURGERY TRIAL SUBSTUDY
pmc-13145602.creator: Axel Wolsink, Floris Schreuder, Jeroen Boogaarts, Erwin Kompanje, Ruben Dammers, Catharina Jm Klijn
pmc-13145602.description: Background and aimsObtaining valid informed consent is not always feasible in acute stroke trials. Although legal and ethical grounds for deferred consent in these situations exist, controversy remains on its proper use and acceptability, especially in trials with more invasive interventions. In this study, we assessed acceptability of deferred consent in an acute neurosurgical intervention trial in intracerebral haemorrhage.

pmc-13228080.title: Development of a stable low-copy mini F plasmid derivative for evaluating β-lactamase substrate specificity through antimicrobial susceptibility testing
pmc-13228080.creator: Haruka Nakagawa Kamura, Kotaro Aoki, Kohji Komori, Kazuhiro Tateda, Yoshikazu Ishii
pmc-13228080.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Traditionally, the impact of the substrate specificity of β-lactamase produced by bacteria on β-lactam resistance (β-lactamase-mediated resistance) has been assessed by performing antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) on transformants carrying the cloned gene on arbitrarily chosen β-lactamase-free plasmid vectors. However, because the promoter strength and plasmid copy number of these vectors are not standardized, the resulting β-lactamase expression levels vary, further hampering cross-study comparisons.

pmc-13297864.title: Microalgae as Novel Food Resources: Technological Breakthroughs, Application Bottlenecks, and Future Pathways
pmc-13297864.creator: Xiaomei Zhang, Weixian Chen, Hui Chen
pmc-13297864.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Global population growth and the demand for sustainable food systems have pushed microalgae into the spotlight as promising novel food resources. They are rich in protein, omega-3 fatty acids, and bioactive pigments including astaxanthin and phycocyanin. Unlike conventional farming, microalgae cultivation can be conducted on non-arable land and may reduce direct competition with conventional food crops for land resources, depending on the production system used.

pmc-13311920.creator: Luc Djousse, Rachel E Ward, Helen Marucci-Wellman, Nedim Yel, Kristin Colson, Abigail A Santos, Mason Coleman-Lopez, Eddie Pan, Tharen Leesch, David Peña, Michelle Congdon, Michele Bolles, David Gagnon, J Michael Gaziano

pmc-13485418.creator: Oinam Somapika Devi, Benjamin Nongrum, Subhankar Paul
pmc-13485418.description: on got affected in the present case. We present a case of a young man in his 30s who sustained a penetrating injury to his right eye lower lid while unloading bamboos from a truck. He came to the outpatient department after 5 days of the injury, when the pain and redness did not subside, and he developed diplopia.

pmc-13582470.title: Parenting concerns among patients with cancer: a qualitative meta-synthesis
pmc-13582470.creator: Yuchen Jiao, Ping Zhu, Liuliu Zhang, Bing Wu
pmc-13582470.description: ObjectivesThis qualitative meta-synthesis aimed to interpret how cancer patients experience and manage parenting concerns, and to identify implications for family-centered psychosocial care.DesignA qualitative meta-synthesis was conducted.MethodsPubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, EBSCO, ProQuest, China Science and Technology Journal Database, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Database were searched from inception to April 2025.

pmc-13629182.title: Biocontrol of watermelon Fusarium wilt caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. niveum with Corallococcus sp. EGB
pmc-13629182.creator: Xinjie Li, Mingze Gao, Zhitao Geng, Minxin Hou, Xiangmin Li, Zhoukun Li
pmc-13629182.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Watermelon Fusarium wilt is a severe soil-borne disease that threatens continuous watermelon production. Effective disease control depends on the differentiation of pathogen races, the accumulation of soil-borne inoculum, and disturbances in the soil bacterial community caused by continuous cropping. In this study, a pathogenic fungus was isolated from diseased watermelon plants in a continuously cropped field in Dongtai, Jiangsu Province, China. Morphological characterization, multigene phylogenetic analysis, and pathogenicity assays revealed that the pathogenic isolate belongs to Fusarium oxysporum f.
